why: The client reported that the delivered file would not import into Premiere Pro (LL-58, registry EP05-G09). It was the private watch page's 'Download MP4': init.mp4 joined to the 79 HLS segments, a fragmented MP4.

what_the_client_received.how: the watch page's join of its streaming package (deliver.joined), rebuilt here from the package that is still in the container
what_the_client_received.evidence: its size equals init.mp4 plus the 79 segments exactly, and equals the size of the file the producer shared; deliver.delivery_problems: fragmented MP4 (moof, mvex, sidx, styp)
what_the_client_received.amends: delivery_manifest.json's note said this rendition was never hashed and is not in the container; its package was in the session's scratch storage, and this is its hash

source.note: the same master the watch page was packaged from (its manifest's source_sha256)

replacement.encode: two-pass x264, preset slow, 3700 kb/s (maxrate 6000k, bufsize 12000k), High@4.0, yuv420p, GOP 48, BT.709 tags; audio stream copied; brand mp42; +faststart

verified.video: H.264 High, level 4.0, 1920x1080, yuv420p, 24/1 constant (r_frame_rate = avg_frame_rate), 11376 frames, 474.000 s: the master's frame count and duration
verified.audio: AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo, 474.000 s; packet MD5 identical to the master's audio stream (17aa20b0dae0a4305e85769e418143ce)
verified.full_decode: ffmpeg decode to null: no errors
verified.frames_viewed: 0:03, 2:00, 5:00 and 7:51 side by side with the master (lead): no visible difference
verified.parts: 17 parts of at most 14 MiB; rejoined byte for byte (deliver.rejoin) and, in headless Chromium, rebuilt by the download page with the same SHA-256 before saving

replacement.not_verified: An import into Premiere Pro itself: the container and codec checks are what an editor needs, but only an import proves it for this file.

watch_page: Republished to stream only; its download button is gone and it links the download page instead (templates/watch.html, test_the_watch_page_no_longer_offers_a_joined_download).

full_quality_copy.why: the producer asked for the full-quality file; the 224 MB replacement had been re-encoded to fit a page version's 256 MB limit and looked to them like the old file
full_quality_copy.how: 34 byte parts of 14 MiB in a private page's asset store (1 GiB quota), rebuilt and SHA-256-checked by the page before saving; the parts were read back and rebuilt to the same hash, and the page was run end to end in headless Chromium
